layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Abstract-The effect of annealing temperature on pitting resistance of 25% Cr duplex UNS S32550 was

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: investigated. CPT and pitting potential were determined for this alloy after annealing at 1020, 1060, 1100 and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 1 140°C. The higher values of CPT and pitting potential were found after annealing at the lower temperatures.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Pitting was always observed preferentially in the ferrite phase. The results can be partially explained by the changes

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in chemical composition of ferrite and austenite phases. Copyright © 1996 Elsevier Science Ltd

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Keywords: A. alloy, A. stainless steel, C. pitting corrosion.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: INTRODUCTION

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The development of duplex stainless steels (DSS) has been linked strongly with the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: increasing requirements of the chemical industry for materials resistance to highly

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: aggressive environments. Duplex stainless steels are widely used in marine environments

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: because of their good resistance to pitting corrosion and stress corrosion cracking. The alloy

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: content and the microstructure are both important variables in determining the pitting

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: corrosion resistance of the DSS. In general, C, P, S and non-metallic inclusions have a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: negative effect on the pitting resistance, whereas Cr, Mo, N, Si and W are beneficial alloying

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: elements against pitting corrosion. A common way to rank the piting susceptibility in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: stainless steels is by the use of the pitting resistance number (PREN).¹Indeed, this idea has

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: begun to be applied to duplex steels in recent years.2,3 The PREN is linked to the content of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: three most important elements Cr, Mo and N, each of them weighted according to its

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: influence on pitting:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Although this is a considerable simplification of elemental influences on corrosion

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: resistance, it has been found to be extremely useful as an index of likely alloy performance

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: purely from the alloy chemical analysis.²

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The difficulty with duplex steels is that there are two phases present with different

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: compositions, with the three key elements partitioned between them (chromium and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: molybdenum are enhanced in the ferrite and nitrogen is enhanced in the austenite). Thus, it

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: is clear³ that a PREN for each phase should be calculated, with the actual performance

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: governed by whichever phase gives the lower figure. Bernhardsson³ has calculated from

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: thermodynamic data how increasing the temperature at which the alloy is annealed can

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: change the compositions and proportions of the two phases. These calculations show that,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: whereas the PREN for ferrite falls with temperature, that for austenite rises, so that there is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: an optimum annealing temperature where the two PREN curves cross. If PREN provides a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: reliable measure of pitting resistance then above this temperature pitting is expected to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: initiate in the ferrite phase and the alloy resistance falls as the PREN for ferrite falls. Below

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the optimum temperature the PREN of ferrite is improving, but the pitting resistance is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: limited by the austenite. The latter will have a smaller PREN than ferrite, and it will further

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: fall with decreasing temperature. Solomon and Devine⁴ have discussed how changing the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: proportions of the two phases influences pitting resistance through altering the phase

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: compositions.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The work described in this paper examines the pitting behaviour of UNS S32550 in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: chloride solutions, in order to determine how changing the ferrite/austenite ratio influences

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pitting resistance for a particular duplex steel, to find the optimum annealing temperature

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: for maximum pitting resistance and whether the site of pitting switches from ferrite to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: austenite above the optimum annealing temperature, as predicted by the theory of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Bernhardsson.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The effect of phase compositions

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the composition profiles show that the ferrite grains are enriched in Cr and Mo and depleted

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in Ni and Cu. Similarly, in the austenite grains the Ni and Cu are enriched, whereas the Cr

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and Mo signals are lower. All elements were evenly distributed within the grains and no

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: segregation of the alloying elements was noticed. The average composition of the important

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: elements in austenite and ferrite in all four samples annealed at 1020, 1060, 1100 and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: are shown in Table 2 together with the average bulk composition of the alloy analysed. The

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: levels of N presented in the ferrite have been assumed to be around 0.05% saturation with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the rest partitioned to the austenite.²

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The first important point to discuss is the relative PREN value of the two phases in each

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sample. The PREN for austenite in sample annealed at

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (36.23) is lower by more than

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: three units than the value of 39.35 calculated for the ferrite, suggesting that pitting should

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: occur only in austenite, but experimental results showed that pitting is confined to the ferrite

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in all samples.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The same is true for samples annealed at 1060 and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: where the PREN for the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ferrite is higher than the austenite by 2.3 and 0.5 units, respectively. Only in the sample

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: annealed at

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: is the PREN of the austenite higher than in the ferrite. As expected, the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: PREN for the ferrite phase decreases as both the annealing temperature and the ferrite

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: content increases, whereas in contrast, the PREN of austenite increases as the annealing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: temperature increases.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Figure 8 also shows the plots of the PREN calculated by using the average composition

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of the alloy (calculated from the analyses shown in Table 2) and the partition coefficients

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: suggested by Charles² compared with the real values calculated directly from the analyses.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The calculated values for ferrite and the real values obtained show good agreement at low

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and high annealing temperatures. The austenite lines shows good agreement at low

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: temperatures, but some deviations at higher temperatures. The discrepancy at high

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: temperatures arises because the partition coefficients of Cr and Mo were found to be

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sensitive to higher annealing temperatures. At lower annealing temperatures, the partition

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: coefficients are less affected by temperature and are closer to those results reported before.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: It has been clearly shown that the pitting resistance of this duplex stainless steel

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: decreases as the annealing temperature is increased consistent with the decreasing PREN for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ferrite; this can be associated with the lower levels of the important alloying elements Mo

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and Cr which partition preferentially to the ferrite, but are diluted as the total concentration

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of ferrite increases.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The important question is whether pitting occurs in ferrite because austenite has higher

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pitting resistance than predicted, or because that for ferrite is lower.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The difference in relative resistance of ferrite and austenite might be influenced by the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: presence of high levels of Cu in the austenite (Table 2) which has been shown to enhance the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pitting resistance of austenitic and duplex stainless steels.7-9 Cu has been suggested to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: improve the pitting resistance of DSS in acid environments,′ and the combination of Cu and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: N is believed to enhance corrosion resistance.8 Further work is in hand to assess

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: experimentally the effect of Cu in the pitting resistance of these steels. On the other hand,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the high levels of sulphur in the ferrite, which are more than double that in the austenite,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: probably reduces the pitting resistance of the ferrite phase. Similarly, the presence of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: phosphorus, which also has been suggested to have detrimental effects on the performance

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of these alloys,1º is higher in the ferrite than in the austenite. Therefore, pitting susceptibility

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: of the ferrite phase may be reduced, relative to the austenite. Certainly, a weighting factor of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: — 123 applied to phosphorus and sulphur in PREN calculations,1º could account for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: preferential pitting of ferrite, but would imply poor performance rather than high pitting

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: resistance, as shown here.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: A full explanation of this behaviour may also require consideration of synergy between

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: elements, rather than considering single elements in isolation. One weakness of the PREN

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The effect of phase compositions

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: approach is that it fails to take such effects into account. Lu et

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: have shown a strong

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: synergism between molybdenum and nitrogen in austenitic stainless steel. In these duplex

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: steels molybdenum levels are highest in the ferrite, but nitrogen levels are much lower than

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in austenite. These enhanced levels of nitrogen could increase the potency of molybdenum

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: such that a lower level of molybdenum actually has greater pit inhibiting power than the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: higher molybdenum content in the ferrite. Further work is needed to establish whether this

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: synergism alone can account for the improved pitting resistance of the austenite phase

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: CONCLUSION

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 1. The pitting potential and CPT of UNS S32550 duplex stainless steel are strongly

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: influenced by the solution treatment temperature. Raising the annealing temperature lowers

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: both parameters. The maximum CPT reached was

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: , obtained by annealing 2 h at

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 1020°C followed by water quenching.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2. Pitting corrosion of UNS S32550 in chloride solutions takes place preferentially in the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ferrite phase rather than in the austenite phase.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3. High annealing temperatures (above

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: increase the ferrite content and dilute

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the key alloying elements in the ferrite lowering the corrosion resistance of the ferrite.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 4. PREN calculated from bulk composition is unlikely to be a good guide to assess

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pitting resistance of duplex stainless steels; a better understanding can be achieved through

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: calculating PREN values for the two phases.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 5. At low annealing temperatures, the partition coefficients of the alloying elements are

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in good agreement with those reported before.² Some deviation from these values is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: observed at higher annealing temperatures (higher ferrite contents).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 6. PREN values for austenite and ferrite calculated from bulk analysis using known

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: partition coefficients can provide a useful first approximation in assessing pitting resistance.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 7. Additional factors beyond the concentration of Cr, Mo and N may need to be

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: considered to fully understand the relative pitting resistances of austenite and ferrite. These

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: could include levels of other beneficial elements such as copper, levels of harmful elements

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: such as sulphur or phosphorus and synergism between elements such as nitrogen and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: molybdenum.
